title: An independent reference sort and LCP check every small input across the build flags
body: Batch 1 of sufr-25f57e. A naive reference sort in the libsufr tests, comparing suffixes byte by byte under the seed mask, max_query_len, dropped N suffixes, softmask and the delimiter, plus a reference LCP by direct comparison of neighbours. Run over 1, 2, 3, abba, smol, mostlya1, mostlya2 and spaced_input in data/inputs under -a, -i, -D, masks 101 11011 1101 10111011, -m 1 3 5 and -n 1 2 3, and once with with_force_64bit. Assert the built suffix array and LCP equal the reference. Replaces the four vacuous *_is_sorted tests in sufr/tests/cli.rs. The open question on LCP above m (sufr-2b76b5) is on the parent.
close_reason: Landed in 9da4b06 as libsufr/tests/oracle.rs, 125 builds at u32. The u64 pass waits on sufr-c549c4. The four vacuous *_is_sorted tests come out under sufr-f5ec10.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/1ddc0e5b
notes.text: sufr-cba493 was closed as not a bug on 2026-11-03, so the LCP of two suffixes inside runs of 1000 or more N is by definition the shorter remaining run, capped at max_query_len. The reference LCP in this oracle computes matched bytes, which is longer when two such runs have equal remaining length and the bytes after them match. No input in the table has two runs of 1000 N, so the two agree on it. An input with such runs needs the shortcut's rule in the reference, not the byte count.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/1ddc0e5b
notes.text: Jack decided on 2026-11-03 to land the oracle at u32 only and fix sufr-c549c4 afterwards, when the table gains a u64 pass.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/1ddc0e5b
notes.text: The u64 pass of the oracle waits on sufr-fde85d, not on sufr-c549c4, which was closed as not a bug.
